name: MUC1-related Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease
aliases: Autosomal Dominant Tubulointerstitial Kidney Disease due to MUC1 mutation

criteria.description: Presence of autosomal dominant inheritance pattern of chronic kidney disease
Identification of pathogenic frameshift mutation in the MUC1 gene
Renal biopsy showing tubulointerstitial fibrosis with minimal glomerular involvement
Progressive chronic kidney disease with bland urinary sediment and absence of significant proteinuria

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of autosomal dominant family history, compatible clinical features, and identification of pathogenic MUC1 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis due to nonspecific clinical and histological findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive chronic kidney disease with bland urinary sediment
searchTerms: chronic kidney failure without urine abnormalities
gradual kidney damage with normal urine tests

pathognomonic.symptomName: Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern of kidney disease
Tubulointerstitial fibrosis on renal biopsy with minimal glomerular involvement
searchTerms: kidney tissue fibrosis with little glomerular damage

common.symptomName: Polyuria and nocturia due to impaired tubular function
searchTerms: frequent urination due to kidney tubule problems
increased urine output and nighttime urination

common.symptomName: Elevated serum creatinine indicating declining renal function

searchTerms: little or no protein in urine

occasional.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: low red blood cells from kidney disease
high uric acid in blood without gout pain
increased blood uric acid without joint inflammation

occasional.symptomName: Mild electrolyte abnormalities (e.g., mild metabolic acidosis)
Fatigue related to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: fatigue linked to chronic kidney failure
low energy due to kidney problems

rare.symptomName: End-stage renal disease requiring dialysis or transplantation
searchTerms: kidney failure requiring transplant or dialysis

rare.symptomName: Secondary hyperparathyroidism due to chronic kidney disease
searchTerms: overactive parathyroid due to kidney disease
high parathyroid hormone from kidney failure

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
Minimal proteinuria and bland urinary sediment
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal to small-sized kidneys with occasional renal cysts
Absence of significant hydronephrosis or obstruction
other: Renal biopsy demonstrating tubulointerstitial fibrosis with minimal glomerular involvement

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent cystic changes on imaging

redFlags: Rapid progression to end-stage renal disease in family members
Absence of significant proteinuria despite worsening renal function
Family history of autosomal dominant kidney disease
references: Eckardt KU, et al. Autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease: diagnosis, classification, and management. Nat Rev Nephrol. 2015.
